title: Secret Reference / Handle
description: An opaque, scoped REFERENCE to a credential held by the secret registry. This document is what a module manifest, a log line, an event, a job and an audit record are permitted to carry. It never carries credential material in `handle`, and no property of this schema is intended to hold any. Note that `correlation_id`, `scope.workspace_id`, `rotation.owner.id` and `revocation.actor.id` are free-text strings: the schema cannot stop a producer pasting a credential into one, so a producer must not.

handle.x-source: Decision Register 5.2 CTR-SEC-001 requires an 'opaque ref'; PT-010 requires that a manifest sees a REFERENCE only. The `secret:` prefix and body charset are ADOPTED FROM CTR-MOD-001 `secret_handles` as PRECEDENT, not as authority: a manifest reference and a registry handle must be the same string or the two contracts do not compose, and shipping a second, different pattern would be a worse defect than the irregularity recorded below. Decision Register 5.2 owns CTR-MOD-001 to A0 and CTR-SEC-001 to A0+A1, so a single-owner contract fixed the syntax of a jointly-owned one with no RFC. That is an OPEN OWNERSHIP CONFLICT for the A1 owner to resolve, recorded in the manifest freeze_boundary and in WP-0A-CON-004 open_blockers. This author must not resolve it.
handle.x-maxlength-note: DECLARED INFERENCE. The baseline states no length. 128 keeps a handle short enough to be an identifier in a log line; it is NOT a control against embedded credential material and must not be read as one.
handle.x-opacity-limitation: THIS PATTERN IS NOT A SECURITY CONTROL, AND MUST NOT BE CITED AS ONE. It excludes mixed-case base64 and nothing else: lowercase hex, lowercase base32 and lowercase dashed bot-token shapes all satisfy it. Independent security review measured the repository secret scanner (scripts/scan-repository-secrets.mjs) against 15 credential bodies this pattern admits and it detected 12. The pattern excludes every format carrying a mandatory uppercase character -- AWS, Meta, Google, JWT, SendGrid, Twilio -- not only mixed-case base64. The residual gap is 5 of 5 lowercase-canonical shapes: bare 32-hex, a UUID, an HMAC hex digest, a passphrase and a dotted-label password. An earlier version of this sentence said the two compose to ZERO coverage; A1 measured it and that was false in the alarming direction, which is as wrong as understating a surface. The real limitation is one of REACH, not of coverage: the scanner walks repository files at commit time and has none over a handle in a log, an event or a job, which is the surface PT-010 is about for a credential smuggled inside a conforming handle body. JSON Schema cannot distinguish a reference from the thing it refers to, and no shape rule available here can, so none is invented. What would close it is a handle ISSUANCE format -- an issuer-assigned, non-secret, non-guessable identifier that a producer cannot mint from credential material -- which the baseline does not specify. A1 (CTR-SEC-001 co-owner) must specify it before freeze. Demonstrated by examples/accepted-gap-structureless-handle-body.json.

scope.x-source: Decision Register 5.2 CTR-SEC-001 requires 'scope'; PT-010 produces a 'scoped credential resolver'; MR-004 produces a 'readiness result per capability/scope', which is why the scope is keyed by capability as well as tenant. The Workspace -> Business Profile -> Page Context nesting is DEC-010 and Workstream 3.1.
scope.x-cross-tenant-limitation: This object records the scope a handle CLAIMS. Nothing here binds the claim to the handle: JSON Schema cannot compare one property's value against another's, so a document -- or a CTR-MOD-001 manifest listing the same handle string -- may assert a scope belonging to a different tenant and this contract will accept it. Independent security review raised exactly this. Enforcement belongs to the resolver named in PT-010, which must reject a resolution whose caller scope does not match the scope the registry recorded when the handle was issued. Declared in untestable_by_schema; NOT claimed as materialized.

ownership.x-source: PT-010 inputs are 'managed/BYOK credentials'; DEC-014 opens Platform AI plus BYOK OpenAI; SEC-012 requires BYOK isolation and provider egress control.

classification.x-source: SEC-003 requires a Public/Internal/Confidential/Restricted matrix in which token and API key are classified. SEC-003 names the four classes but has NOT yet assigned the class a credential handle carries, so this contract enumerates the four and pins none. See accepted_gaps in the manifest.

state.x-source: Decision Register 5.2 CTR-SEC-001 requires 'rotation/revoke'; SEC-005 requires a secret to be 'encrypted, masked, rotated'; PT-010 requires that revocation is possible immediately.

resolvable.x-source: DECLARED INFERENCE from PT-010 'revoke immediately' and MR-004 'missing secret/scope/entitlement does not activate'. The baseline states revocation as a runtime effect; the only contract-level expression of it is whether the registry will still resolve this handle to a credential. Inferred from PT-010 and MR-004; not a field named in either.

owner.x-source: INF-006 requires 'rotation owner/date complete'. The owner is a TYPED reference rather than a free string because Workstream 3.1 forbids a free-string actor. The two kinds are the two credential ownerships PT-010 names: platform-managed and BYOK.

rotation.x-source: INF-006 'rotation owner/date complete'; SEC-005 requires the secret to be rotated.

redaction.x-source: PT-010 requires that logs, events and jobs contain no secret; SEC-005 requires that browser, job, event and log never see plaintext; SEC-012 requires that a key does not enter analytics or an error trace. Each surface is a separate const true, so a document asserting that any one of them is unsafe is not a valid secret handle. Decision Register 5.2 lists 'redaction tests' as a freeze artifact.

revocation.x-source: PT-010 requires immediate revocation; SEC-009 requires that a CREDENTIAL action records actor and correlation. The reason is a stable key rather than prose because CTR-ERR-001 establishes Thai message keys for anything a person reads; that key-not-prose choice is a DECLARED INFERENCE from CTR-ERR-001 and CM-004.

correlation_id.x-source: SEC-009 requires actor AND correlation on a credential action; OB-001 requires one trace across the workflow.

allOf.x-rule: PT-010 'revoke immediately' plus SEC-009 credential auditing: a revoked handle must no longer resolve, and must record when, by whom and why it was revoked.

PT-010 and MR-004: an active handle is one the resolver will still resolve, and a handle carrying a revocation record is not active. `rotating` is deliberately left unconstrained on `resolvable` because the baseline states no rotation-overlap rule; see freeze_boundary.
PT-010 distinguishes managed from BYOK credentials and INF-006 requires a named rotation owner: a platform-managed credential is rotated by a platform role.
PT-010 managed/BYOK split with SEC-012 BYOK isolation: a customer-supplied key is rotated by the workspace that supplied it, not by a platform role.

PT-010 'revoke immediately': a handle that carries a revocation record must not resolve, whatever its `state` says. allOf[0] binds this to `state: revoked` and allOf[1] keeps a revocation record off an `active` handle; without this clause a `rotating` handle could carry a complete revocation record and still declare `resolvable: true`, which is the revoked-but-still-resolving case PT-010 exists to forbid. Raised by A1 in security co-owner review of the Candidate promotion.
